entries.test: Public evaluations of computer vision available in October 2023 would show whether substantial ordinary visual tasks remained unsolved.
entries.note: The claim concerns the field as of publication, not current capabilities.

entries.test: Published evaluations of contemporary LLMs against the human-comparable flexibility, resourcefulness, and reliability criteria stated in the post would settle whether they qualified.
entries.note: The following paragraphs supply the otherwise ambiguous AGI criteria.

entries.test: Public comparisons of October 2023 AI systems with human performance across varied cognitive tasks would test their generality and reliability.
entries.note: The author explicitly adopts the definition to which 'this' refers.

entries.test: Contemporary public arithmetic, kinship, chess, factual-writing, and driving evaluations would test the listed capability limitations and whether human-level driving had been demonstrated.
entries.note: The proposition turns 'we have yet to see' human-level driving into an inability claim. It also removes the factual-writing context from the fabrication claim.

entries.test: The cited article's definitions and arguments, compared with the criteria stated here and contemporary capability evidence, would test whether it lowers the threshold and whether its premises support its conclusion.
entries.note: The post identifies specific arguments and a comparison standard, making this more than an unspecified dismissal.

entries.test: Public human-comparison evaluations of October 2023 systems on the listed language tasks would show whether those systems performed them competently.
entries.note: The listed tasks give the competence claim a practical test despite the absence of numerical thresholds.

entries.test: A publicly documented comparison of the first author's nine-year-old and a contemporary LLM on matched five-digit multiplication problems would settle the comparison.
entries.note: The source identifies a particular child; the proposition drops that identifying restriction. A lack of published results would not make the comparison inherently uncheckable.
The author explicitly frames the need for further paradigm shifts as more likely, not certain.
Planning and world-model weaknesses are separately testable. The combined claim retains a tentative inference that missing AGI ingredients are 'strongly suggest[ed]'.
The main assertion judges the opposing conclusion as overreach; the concession about prerequisites is explicitly tentative.

entries.test: Contemporary language and multimodal evaluations, assessed against the post's stated general-intelligence criteria, would test the performance comparison and whether it establishes those criteria.
entries.note: Although credited to the other authors, the performance premise is explicitly accepted as fact.

entries.test: Architecture descriptions of October 2023 state-of-the-art systems in the named domains would show how extensively they used transformers.
entries.note: The domain list provides concrete targets for checking the claim.

entries.test: Public deployment reports and comparative evaluations from the period would show whether practitioners frequently used alternative methods with substantially better tractability, reliability, and efficiency.
entries.note: The source says 'far more' on all three dimensions; the proposition weakens these comparisons to merely 'more'.

entries.test: Public capability and deployment evidence across the practical domains named in the paragraph would test whether transformers and generative AI functioned as broadly applicable substitutes for other methods.
entries.note: The proposition removes the qualification that the rejected all-purpose capability is the one some people imagine. The surrounding examples nevertheless provide a testable capability reading.
Neither whose understanding is at issue nor what would count as understanding the scope is specified. 'Remarkable' supplies no shared threshold.

entries.test: Public deployment results and reliability evaluations compared with prevalent contemporary claims about useful LLM applications would test both practical usefulness and its alleged overstatement.
entries.note: The comparison is broad, but has a plain reading about demonstrated uses versus advertised uses.

entries.test: Public evaluations and documented applications of the generation following October 2023 systems would show whether capabilities and applications expanded and existing weaknesses diminished.
entries.note: Adding 'only' imposes a stronger ceiling on improvement than the source states. Subsequent generations existed by the evaluation date.

entries.test: Public capability evidence available in October 2023 would show whether any contemporary technology met the human-comparable generality and reliability criteria stated in the post.
entries.note: Read in context, this rejects an evidentiary claim under specified AGI criteria.
